title: Technology — high band (~8.0)
notes: Near C1 oral resourcefulness; still not 'expert' 9.0.

turns.text: How has technology changed the way people learn languages?
It has democratised access. Learners can rehearse pronunciation with feedback apps, shadow native speakers on demand, and join communities that would have been unreachable a decade ago.
Absolutely. Algorithmic feeds can trap people in simplified content, and over-reliance on instant translation may delay the hard work of retrieving vocabulary under pressure.
What role should teachers play now?
Teachers become curators and coaches. They diagnose fossilised errors, design tasks that force spontaneous speech, and help learners interpret feedback that machines cannot contextualise.
